plugins.name: wovenflow
plugins.description: Doc-Test-Driven Development (DTDD) — literate-programming-flavored TDD. Eight skills: designflow (Design phase — write .spec.md with user stories + ∵ IF / ↦ WHEN / ∴ THEN behaviors, prose only; invokes redteam before locking), testflow (Test phase — insert inline test blocks; bundled extractor produces derived test files at pre-test time; 28 built-in languages + override flags for any other language or DSL), subflow (Build phase — dispatch implementer subagents per behavior with spec-compliance and code-quality review; Team mode when CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, Parallel mode otherwise, Sequential as rare fallback; final step invokes scopecheck), scopecheck (coverage-based over-implementation guardrail — any committed line not exercised by a test is by-construction not required by any behavior; verdicts CLEAN/VIOLATIONS/AMBIGUOUS/BLOCKED, with per-region resolution proposals to remove or formalize), researchflow (pre-design phase — bridges the gap between the agent's training cutoff and current reality via web search; composes researcher profiles for academic, competitive-landscape, and custom fields), redteam (decision-quality gate — list the top three reasons this is not the right call; invocable at any commit point), setup (interactive workflow wizard — detects existing CLAUDE.md workflow, walks through each phase suggesting skills or crafting custom ones from bundled scaffold templates: claim, startup, verify, ship-pr, ship-direct, wrap-up, researcher, tasks.py, prior-work, and the split findings/sessions logs), and flowtune (workflow self-tuning — reviews the session for friction signals and proposes updates to CLAUDE.md's Standard workstream so future sessions have the right defaults). Involvement modes (minimal / standard / maximal / custom) control how often the workflow stops to ask the user, and `build.implementer` (fork / subagent / inline) controls who writes the code in the Build phase; both are configured in `.wovenflow.yml` at the project root. Projects keep three capped, purpose-split records: a findings index read at every session start, an unbounded session ledger read at none, and a prior-work index of external sources so a claim is never written from recollection when a source exists.
